correctness.rationale: For the full labelled length-three count law, E(C_i)/3 identifies the positive stationary mass; the all-i event identifies the nonnegative loop q_i by its square. Flow conservation makes the three symmetric edge-flow sums the unique solution of the three incident-sum equations. The (2i,1j) event has probability q_i S_ij + pi_i P_ij P_ji by enumerating its three paths. The product of the two flows and their sum determine their absolute difference; zero divergence identifies the oriented differences on 12,23,31 as one common signed current. No step divides by a possibly zero transition: only pi_i is a required nonzero denominator. Both signs are realized by the given chain and its stationary reverse, which have identical counts by path reversal (one matrix if the current is zero). Diagonal similarity of the transpose preserves every indexed principal minor of P and I-P. The strictly positive circulant example has six equiprobable two-visit counts at both delta values and minors 3/16 and 13/64. For two states, same-state two-visit counts recover the loops and hence the rows; at one visit the symmetric two-state family with variable positive switching rate has constant stationary law. This is identification from a population law, not estimation from one path.
